chunks: 3025 - And Jamīl ibn Darrāj narrated from him that he said:
“There is no harm in a man departing during the first departure, then remaining in Mecca.”
And he said: “My father عليه السلام used to say: Whoever wishes may stone the Jamarāt at the rise of the day, then depart.”
He said: So I said to him, “Until when does the stoning of the Jamarāt remain?” He said: “From the rise of the day until sunset. And whoever has taken game may not depart during the first departure.”

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعَ النَّهَارِ: the rise or height of the day
key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: game or hunted animal taken while in ihram-related context
key_terms.النَّفْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: the first departure from Minā during hajj rites
key_terms.رَمَى الْجِمَارَ: performed the stoning of the Jamarāt
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the end time mentioned for the ruling
key_terms.يُقِيمَ بِمَكَّةَ: to remain in Mecca after departing

ai.seo_question: When can the Jamarāt be stoned, and who is not allowed to depart in the first nafr from Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives rulings related to departure from Minā during the first nafr and the time for stoning the Jamarāt. It states that stoning may be done from the rise of the day until sunset, and that one who has hunted game may not leave in the first departure.
